cards.front: What should you remember from A Tale of Three Intersecting Lines?
cards.back: A TALE OF THREE 7 INTERSECTING LINES A triangle is the most basic closed shape.

cards.front: What should you remember from A Tale of Three Intersecting Lines?
cards.back: As we know, it consists of: • three corner points, that we call the vertex of the triangle, and • three line segments or the sides of the triangle that join the pairs of vertices.

cards.front: What should you remember from A Tale of Three Intersecting Lines?
cards.back: B A U X Y Z B ∆ YZX A W C ∆ ABC V ∆WUV ∆BAU U Observe the symbol used to denote a triangle and how the triangles are named using their vertices.

cards.front: What should you remember from A Tale of Three Intersecting Lines?
cards.back: While naming a triangle, the vertices can come in any order.

cards.front: What should you remember from A Tale of Three Intersecting Lines?
cards.back: The three sides meeting at the corners give rise to three angles that we call the angles of the triangle.

cards.front: What should you remember from A Tale of Three Intersecting Lines?
cards.back: For example, in ∆ABC, these angles are ∠CAB, ∠ABC, ∠BCA, which we simply denote as ∠A, ∠B and ∠C, respectively.

cards.front: What should you remember from A Tale of Three Intersecting Lines?
cards.back: What happens when the three vertices lie on a straight line?

cards.front: What should you remember from A Tale of Three Intersecting Lines?
cards.back: 7.1 Equilateral Triangles Among all the triangles, the equilateral triangles are the most symmetric ones.
